title: Fields' bandleading philosophy: the band is the show
summary: He never pushed himself as soloist, featured his men and learned from T. Holder that nobody is better than the person beside them.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: I guess why they said that, I guess through some vision I always knew that it was the band that was the show and if you look at some of the press material, I never was any sensational soloist and never did try, but I didn't try to be a one-man band, and they would always say, when one had the ability, he was introduced and he was featured and even if he wasnt a star, I would let you know he was in my band, and I tried to always-- my arrangements, I would talk to them. One reason that I got along with Rene Hall, he arranged after he left and we were pretty tight, I would tell him how I would like for this to

be fixed when we were talking, and If I had a man in the band and if he was good enough to be in my band and he's getting paid (inaudible) and that's the way that I did and I would always let him know that if he was there, he was important.

That was one thing that I learned when I was first starting from T. Holder. If you're in there, you're not all that much better than the person you're sitting beside of and I guess when the men knew that that was the way I was, I guess they stood by me.
